title: Chickpea Curry
subtitle: Quick dry-style chickpea curry with tomatoes and spices
excerpt: Tinned chickpeas cooked with tomatoes, onion, and a short list of spices into a thick, textured curry. Ready in 30 minutes. Vegan, gluten-free, and deeply satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chickpeas with tomatoes and spices appear in various forms across South Asian cooking: chana masala is the Punjabi version with its characteristic sour notes from amchur (dried mango powder) or tamarind, while the milder British-adapted version uses the same base spices without the souring agents. This quick stovetop version uses tinned chickpeas for convenience. The key is frying the spices long enough in the oil to bloom their flavour before adding the tomatoes.

content.text: Fry the spices in the oil for a full minute after adding them: this blooms the ground spices and removes the raw flavour. The chickpeas go in drained but keep the tin open: if the sauce looks too thick, add a splash of the chickpea liquid to loosen it.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onions and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deep golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, and chilli powder. Stir and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the tinned tomatoes and salt. Simmer for 10 minutes until thickened. Add the drained chickpeas. Cook for a further 5 to 8 minutes until the chickpeas are heated through and coated in the sauce.
Add the lemon juice. Taste and season. Scatter with fresh coriander. Serve with rice or flatbreads.
